items.prompt_latex: A car travels a distance of 100 m in 5 seconds. Calculate the speed of the car.
hint_ladder: What is the distance and time given?
Substitute the values into the formula.
items.targets_because: This item requires the student to perform a calculation explicitly, addressing the lack of calculations seen in the misconception.

items.prompt_latex: An object is dropped from a height of 45 m. Calculate the time it takes to reach the ground. (Assume \( g = 9.81 \text{ m/s}^2 \))
hint_ladder: Identify the height and acceleration due to gravity.
Use the formula for free fall time.
Substitute the height and gravity values into the formula.
items.targets_because: This item reinforces the need for calculations by requiring the student to compute time from given height and gravity.

items.prompt_latex: A spring stretches 0.5 m when a force of 10 N is applied. Calculate the spring constant \( k \) and its uncertainty if the force has an uncertainty of 0.5 N.
items.solution_latex: \( k = \frac{F}{x} = \frac{10 \text{ N}}{0.5 \text{ m}} = 20 \text{ N/m} \) and uncertainty \( \Delta k = k \cdot \frac{\Delta F}{F} = 20 \cdot \frac{0.5}{10} = 1 \text{ N/m} \)
hint_ladder: What is the formula for spring constant?
Identify the values for force and displacement.
Calculate the uncertainty based on the formula.
items.targets_because: This problem explicitly requires students to perform calculations for both the spring constant and its uncertainty, addressing the misconception directly.

items.prompt_latex: A projectile is launched at an angle of 30 degrees with an initial velocity of 20 m/s. Calculate the horizontal range and the uncertainty in the range if the velocity has an uncertainty of 1 m/s.
items.solution_latex: \( R = \frac{v^2 \sin(2\theta)}{g} = \frac{(20 \text{ m/s})^2 \sin(60)}{9.81} \approx 40.82 \text{ m} \) and uncertainty \( \Delta R = R \cdot \frac{2 \Delta v}{v} \approx 40.82 \cdot \frac{2 \cdot 1}{20} \approx 4.08 \text{ m} \)
hint_ladder: What is the formula for the range of a projectile?
Identify the angle and initial velocity.
Calculate the uncertainty using the given uncertainty in velocity.
items.targets_because: This extension problem challenges the student to apply calculations in a more complex scenario, reinforcing the importance of calculations and uncertainty.
